name: Al Rajhi Bank
legal_name: Al Rajhi Banking and Investment Corporation (a Saudi Joint Stock Company)
founded: Roots in 1957 (fact sheet); formed and licensed as a joint stock company under Royal Decree No. M/59 dated 29 June 1987; CR 1010000096
ownership_summary: Tadawul-listed bank, chaired by Abdullah bin Sulaiman Al Rajhi; two Al Rajhi family members sit on the board (S2). Holders above 5% could not be verified: the Saudi Exchange major-shareholders page returned 403 and Argaam's shareholder table is behind a login. The EGM of 20 Apr 2026 approved a 1-for-2 bonus issue, raising share capital from SAR 40bn (4,000m shares) to SAR 60bn (6,000m shares) (S3 note 14). Market capitalisation was SAR 395.4bn at 30 Jun 2026 (S5).
government_link: No direct government shareholding found in the sources reviewed. Major-shareholder register not accessible (see open_items).
group_structure: Parent bank with the Saudi branch network plus foreign branches in Kuwait and Jordan and a Malaysian Islamic bank subsidiary. Subsidiaries at 30 Jun 2026 (S3 note 1): Al Rajhi Capital Company (100%; CMA-licensed dealing/brokerage, asset management, advising, arranging, custody; profiled separately as sa-alrajhi-capital), Emkan Finance (100%; micro consumer and SME finance), International Digital Solutions Co. / Neoleap (100%; payments, urpay wallet), Neotek (100%; open banking, SAMA-authorised), Drahim Holdings (67.48%; PFM and automated investment), Ejada Systems (90%; IT services; classified held for sale with a planned private placement and IPO), Tawtheeq (100%), Tuder Real Estate (100%), Management and Development for Human Resources Co. (100%), Al Rajhi Financial Markets Ltd (Cayman, 100%) and Al Rajhi Corporation Limited (Malaysia, 100%). The bank also holds an associate (carrying value SAR 1,270m). Double counting: Al Rajhi Capital's revenue and AUM sit inside the bank's 'Investment services, brokerage and other' segment; do not add sa-alrajhi-capital figures to this record.

footprint: Saudi Arabia plus Malaysia, Jordan and Kuwait. 547 branches at 30 Jun 2026 including foreign branches (S3 note 1). The fact sheet gives 513 branches in KSA plus 13 in Malaysia, 13 in Jordan and 2 in Kuwait, 4,273 ATMs, 990k+ POS terminals and 135 remittance centres (S5, S8). Six Private Banking centres: Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Makkah, Dammam and Qassim (S19).
customer_segments: Retail mass ('Classic experience'), youth and expatriates; Affluent and Diamond Affluent tiers (the AR calls this the 'Premium' segment); Private Banking (HNW); MSME; large corporate; financial institutions (S10, S19-S21, S46).
business_lines: Four reportable segments (S3 note 19): Retail (H1 2026 operating income SAR 10.2bn); Corporate incl. MSME and VIP deposits (SAR 5.9bn); Treasury (SAR 4.2bn); 'Investment services, brokerage and other' (SAR 1.12bn), which covers mutual funds, local and international share trading and investment portfolios run through Al Rajhi Capital. Private Banking is a separate executive function (Chief Private Banking Officer). Other group businesses: payments (Neoleap/urpay), consumer and SME finance (Emkan), open banking (Neotek), robo/PFM (Drahim), and investment banking through Al Rajhi Capital. All products are Shariah-compliant.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Al Rajhi Bank is fully Shariah-compliant. Its investment business sits in the 100%-owned Al Rajhi Capital: AUM of SAR 165,822m at end-2025 (+34.5%), second-largest asset manager in KSA, and the leading Tadawul broker by value traded (S4, S9). The bank sells wealth through three published tiers. Affluent: SAR 250k opening deposit, SAR 100k average balance, SAR 20k salary, or SAR 1m relationship with Al Rajhi Capital. Diamond Affluent: SAR 1m, 500k, 40k or SAR 2m with Al Rajhi Capital. Private Banking: no threshold published; six centres and a dedicated RM, with investment products 'offered to you through AlRajhi Capital' (S19-S21). A Chief Private Banking Officer, not in the AR 2025 executive list, now sits on the executive team (S1). The bank owns 67.48% of Drahim, a robo/PFM platform whose robo portfolios passed 1.5bn in investments (currency not stated) and which launched Drahim Business with 30+ funds in Sep 2025 (S3, S14). Al Rajhi Capital also runs the 'alrajhi Mashora' robo-advisory service (S9). The 'Harmonize the Group' strategy ends in 2026, and a new 3-year strategy is being prepared (S7).

segments.name: Affluent
segments.eligibility: Any one of: new account opened with SAR 250k+; 3-month average balance SAR 100,000+; monthly salary transfer SAR 20,000+; total relationship value SAR 1m+ with Al Rajhi Capital (as published). Affluent centres in branches; free Visa Signature card.

segments.name: Diamond Affluent
segments.eligibility: Any one of: new account opened with SAR 1m+; 3-month average balance SAR 500,000+; monthly salary transfer SAR 40,000+; total relationship value SAR 2m+ with Al Rajhi Capital (as published). Dedicated relationship manager; fee exemption; Infinite card.

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: Not published. Dedicated relationship manager; investment products through AlRajhi Capital; credit facilities to support investments; 6 Private Banking centres.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking proposition with a dedicated RM, 'investment products and services offered to you through AlRajhi Capital', 'financial solutions and credit facilities to support investments', and 6 Private Banking centres in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Makkah, Dammam and Qassim (S19). Led by a Chief Private Banking Officer on the executive committee (S1). The AR strategy section also mentions 'exclusive Private Banking services for high-net-worth clients' for corporate clients (S15). No PB client or asset figures published.

asset_management.detail: Through Al Rajhi Capital: AUM SAR 165,822m at 31 Dec 2025 (2024: 123,319m), ranked #2 in KSA. Al Rajhi Awaeed Fund is the largest public mutual fund in KSA. The 2025 'Fund Factory' launched private funds, and real estate launched 13+ private funds of SAR 25.8bn+. The bank also runs Mudaraba funds through its Investment Department (FS note). See sa-alrajhi-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through Al Rajhi Capital: 15.5% market share by value traded at end-2025 (AR); the 2Q26 presentation shows '+13%' market share of value traded. 25.2% share of the Kingdom's digital trading market; Super App (3m+ downloads) and Super Web; options across 38 international markets; fully digital margin lending.

digital_investing.detail: AR 2025: Al Rajhi Capital's 'investment options are integrated into the alrajhi bank app'. The bank site offers 'Investment funds' (equity, growth, savings, balanced, real estate, endowment) funded from current account, Visa or Apple Pay, plus a Systematic Investment Plan (fixed monthly investment into a chosen fund) (S22-S24). Equities, IPOs and international trading run in the separate Al Rajhi Capital Super App/Super Web. Drahim (67.48%) offers robo portfolios and a Drahim Investment Card issued by the bank with Al Rajhi Capital investments (S14). A new lifestyle money-management app, 'nera', is run as an Al Rajhi Bank channel (S41).

advisory.detail: Al Rajhi Capital is CMA-licensed for advising (S3 note 1); Private Banking and Diamond Affluent have dedicated RMs (S19, S21); Al Rajhi Capital has a Head of Wealth and Institutional Clients (S42).

discretionary.detail: Al Rajhi Capital lists 'Discretionary Portfolio Management' under asset management (S44). Size not disclosed.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Two in-group robo offers. (1) Al Rajhi Capital's 'alrajhi Mashora', an automated, algorithm-driven investment service (AR 2025). (2) Drahim, a 67.48% subsidiary and 'financial management and automated investment platform' under SAMA and CMA licences. Its robo portfolios passed 1.5bn in investments (currency not stated); it launched Rent and Dividend portfolios and, in Sep 2025, Drahim Business with 30+ local and global funds.

funds_platform.detail: In-house Al Rajhi Capital funds sold through the bank site/app and the Al Rajhi Capital app. Drahim Business offers 'more than 30 local and global investment funds' (managers not named). No third-party fund platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: No client-facing structured products found on Private Banking, Affluent or Investment pages. The bank holds 'FVOCI sukuk and structured products investments' on its own balance sheet (S3), which is not a client offering.

private_markets.detail: Al Rajhi Capital private funds: PE/financing funds launched by its Fund Factory in 2025 and 13+ private real estate funds (SAR 25.8bn+); exited a SAR 1bn+ private fund. Access for Private Banking clients is via Al Rajhi Capital.

islamic_wealth.detail: The whole group is Shariah-compliant under a Shari'a Authority (S3 note 1). Shariah funds, Murabaha customer time investments, Mudaraba funds, Al Rajhi Awaeed money market fund, and sukuk (Al Rajhi Capital is a primary dealer for Saudi government sukuk).

Q2-26 call: CEO said 2026 is the last year of 'Harmonize the Group' and 'we are in the process of preparing our next 3-year strategy'; fee growth drivers included 'investment banking and assets under management'

opportunities: Strategy reset: the CEO said on 28 Jul 2026 that the bank is 'preparing our next 3-year strategy' to replace 'Harmonize the Group', which ends in 2026 (S7 p.14).

Wealth leadership is new: a Chief Private Banking Officer (Hani Al Meghem) and a Chief Strategy Officer (Abid Shakeel) appear on the Oct 2026 executive page but not in the AR 2025 executive list (S1, S11). The digital head is acting (S1).
Affluent eligibility already counts Al Rajhi Capital relationship value (SAR 1m Affluent, SAR 2m Diamond), so bank and investment propositions are linked (S20, S21).

The bank's own investment pages list only 'Investment funds' and a 'Systematic Investment Plan'; Private Banking lists investment products only via Al Rajhi Capital, with no model portfolios or international/alternatives offer on the bank side (S19, S22-S24).
Very large digital base: 21.7m customers, a 96:4 digital-to-manual ratio and 75% of active customers on digital channels (S5, S17). Al Rajhi Capital's Super App has 3m+ downloads (S9).
On the Q2-26 call, the CFO named assets under management as a fee-income growth driver (S7 p.5).
barriers: Islamic-only group: all products need Shari'a Authority approval (S3 note 1).
In-group robo and model portfolios already exist: Al Rajhi Capital's 'alrajhi Mashora' robo service and the 67.48%-owned Drahim automated investment platform (S9, S14).

Investment licences sit in Al Rajhi Capital (CMA licence 07068/37), the #2 asset manager with a large in-house fund factory and private real estate funds, so product contracts would likely be with the subsidiary (S9, S44).
Strong in-house tech group: Ejada (systems integration, being sold down), Neoleap (payments), Neotek (open banking) (S3).
